title: Conduct Standard 1 of 2018 — Criteria for Authorisation of OTC Derivatives Providers
signatory: Abel Moffat Sithole, for the Financial Sector Conduct Authority
sourceNote: FSCA Conduct Standard 1 of 2018 published 27 July 2018 under FMA s.6(8)(a). Sets out the criteria an applicant must satisfy to be authorised as an OTC derivative provider (ODP), and the ongoing obligations of an authorised ODP. Applies to all categories of ODP applicant; banks apply via Application Index 1.

sections.title: Enabling authority and publication
sections.text:
The Financial Sector Conduct Authority, hereby under section 6(8)(a) of the Financial Markets Act, 2012 (Act No. 19 of 2012), prescribe criteria for authorisation as an OTC derivative provider as set out in the Schedule.

ABEL MOFFAT SITHOLE
For THE FINANCIAL SECTOR CONDUCT AUTHORITY
Date of publication: 27 July 2018

sections.title: Definitions
sections.text:
In this Schedule, "the Act" means the Financial Markets Act, 2012 (Act No. 19 of 2012), and "the Regulations" means the Regulations prescribed under the Act, and any word or expression to which a meaning has been assigned in the Act or the Regulations bears the meaning so assigned to it, and unless the context otherwise indicates—

"provider" has the same meaning as "authorised OTC derivative provider"; and

"senior manager" means a member of senior management or the person in charge of the unit or division that carries on the business of the provider.

subsections.text: (1) A juristic person may apply to the Authority to be authorised as a provider.

(2) An applicant for authorisation as a provider must submit a written application on Form FM 6 accompanied by the information—
(a) specified in Annexure 1 to Form FM 6; and
(b) required in respect of members of the controlling body and every senior manager of the provider specified in Annexure 2 to Form FM 6.

Address
Applications must be submitted to:

sections.title: Criteria for authorisation
sections.text: Section 4 sets out four main criteria categories that every applicant and provider must satisfy on an ongoing basis.

subsections.text:
(2)(a) A provider must furnish the Authority with a quarterly report detailing the calculation of the required liquid net assets, calculated in terms of this Standard and the measures taken to obtain additional funding, if necessary.

(b) If the Authority is not satisfied that such liquid net assets are sufficient to cover the risks involved, the Authority may require a provider to obtain additional liquid assets funded by equity over a time period as determined by the Authority.

sections.title: Fit and Proper Requirements
sections.text: An applicant and a provider must satisfy the Authority that it complies with the following fit and proper requirements:

subsections.text: (1) A member of the controlling body and every senior manager of an applicant and a provider must be a person who is honest and has integrity.

(2) In determining whether a member of the controlling body or a senior manager of an applicant and a provider complies with subparagraph (1), the Authority may refer to any information in possession of the Authority or brought to the Authority's attention.

(4) An applicant, and a member of the controlling body or a senior manager of an applicant must in the application be candid and accurate and must of own accord disclose all facts or information at the disposal of, or which may be accessible to the applicant, a member of the controlling body or a senior manager and which may be relevant for purposes of a decision by the Authority whether the provider, the members of the controlling body or the senior manager complies with subparagraph (1).
(5) A provider must submit its application with completed Annexure B and C Forms in respect of each of the members of the controlling body and senior managers.

(1) An applicant and a provider must satisfy the Authority that the members of the controlling body or senior managers have the competency to undertake the relevant duties and functions of the provider, and where appropriate, detailed knowledge of the structure, purpose and risks of the OTC derivatives associated with the duty or function.

(2) To demonstrate competence, a member of the controlling body or a senior manager involved in carrying out the applicable duties and functions must act in a knowledgeable, professional and efficient manner.

(3) Without limiting the generality of subparagraph (1), in determining a person's competence, the Authority may have regard to the following matters:
(a) the person's past performance or expertise in the nature of the business being conducted;
(b) the person's skills and experience to understand, operate and manage the regulated activities and financial affairs; and
(c) the person's technical knowledge and ability to perform prescribed duties for which he or she is engaged, including recognised professional qualifications and membership of relevant professional institutions.

sections.title: Operational ability

subsections.text: (1) An applicant and a provider may not be in liquidation or in provisional liquidation, or subject to business rescue proceedings as contemplated in the Companies Act, or have made arrangements with creditors, or filed for winding-up.
(2) The assets of the applicant and the provider (excluding goodwill and other intangible assets) must exceed its liabilities (excluding loans validly subordinated in favour of all other creditors).

(3) A provider—
(a) must maintain current assets which are at least sufficient to meet current liabilities; and
(b) may not be subject to any judgment debt or award that remains outstanding or has not been satisfied within a reasonable period.

sections.title: Financial soundness of members of the controlling body or senior managers
sections.text:
A member of the controlling body or senior manager of a provider may not be—
(a) an unrehabilitated insolvent or subject to debt review as contemplated by the National Credit Act, 2005 (Act No. 34 of 2005); and
(b) subject to any judgment debt or award that remains outstanding or has not been satisfied within a reasonable period.

subsections.text:
(1) A provider must organise and control its affairs responsibly and effectively, with—
(a) sound risk management principles, that takes into account—
(i) its risk appetite, risk profile, market and macroeconomic conditions; and
(ii) the risk of a significant deterioration in market liquidity; and
(b) prudent policies and processes, systems and resources, approved by its controlling body, to identify, measure, evaluate, monitor, report and control or mitigate risks on a timely basis.

(2) The provider's controlling body is responsible to oversee management of the provider in such a way that ensures that the policies and processes are implemented effectively and fully integrated into the provider's management process.
(5) A provider must conduct a regular review to ensure that it maintains adequate policies, procedures and controls.
(6) A provider must take reasonable steps to document all material systems and controls and the relevant documentation must be kept up to date, and be signed off by the controlling body annually.
(7) An applicant and a provider must be able to describe and demonstrate the objectives and operation of its risk management procedures and its systems and controls to the Authority.

(8) The Authority may request an additional capital amount to be held if the provider fails to satisfy the condition stipulated in sub-paragraph 4(d) to the satisfaction of the Authority or fails to demonstrate that the provider has a sufficient number of sufficiently skilled staff in the provider's trading area, risk control, audit or independent review function, or the back-office.
(9) A provider must conduct an appropriate independent review of the provider's risk measurement system at regular intervals but not less frequent than once a year.

sections.title: Compliance function
Business continuity planning
sections.text:
An applicant and a provider must—
(a) maintain a business continuity plan which adequately identifies and mitigates material business continuity risks faced by the provider; and
(b) regularly test the effectiveness of the continuity plan and address any deficiencies.

sections.title: Record keeping and data retention
Suspension and termination of authorisation
sections.text: Section 5 covers both involuntary termination (s5.1 — Authority-initiated on grounds of non-compliance, cessation, false information, or failure to comply) and voluntary termination (s5.2 — provider-initiated, 30 days prior notice). Involuntary process requires notice, opportunity to respond, and Authority decision. Urgent provisional suspension available where substantial prejudice to clients or the public may occur.

subsections.text:
(2) Before suspending or terminating any authorisation, the Authority must—
(a) inform the provider of the intention to suspend or terminate such authorisation and the grounds for suspension or termination; and
(b) give the provider a reasonable opportunity to make a submission in response.

(5) Despite the provisions of sub-paragraph (2), the Authority may under urgent circumstances, where the Authority is satisfied on reasonable grounds that substantial prejudice to clients or the general public may occur, provisionally suspend the authorisation of a provider.

(8) A person whose authorisation has been terminated under this section is prohibited from carrying on the business of an OTC derivative provider for a period specified by the Authority and from applying for a new authorisation.
(1) A provider may voluntarily terminate its authorisation by making a submission to the Authority at least 30 days prior to such termination.

(2) The Authority may—
(a) accept such termination unconditionally; or
(b) terminate the authorisation subject to such measures as the Authority may determine for the protection of the interests of clients of the provider.

sections.title: Commencement and short title
sections.text: This Standard comes into operation on the date of publication and is called the Criteria for authorisation for OTC derivative providers.

sections.title: Application form for authorisation as an OTC derivative provider
sections.text: Form FM 6 is the standard application form submitted by the CEO of the applicant entity under FMA s.6(8)(a). Must be accompanied by Annexure 1 (entity and operational information) and Annexure 2 (controlling body member information).

sections.title: Information required in an application for authorisation as an OTC derivative provider
sections.text: Requires: (1) administrative information — addresses, contact numbers, persons exercising control, controlling body list, bank/auditor/attorney details; (2) copy of founding documents; (3) adequacy of financial resources — audited AFS, 3-year budgets, funding arrangements; (4) adequacy of management and human resources — org structure, CVs, staffing projections; (5) business plan — IT systems, risk management approach, market integrity, security procedures, corporate governance; (6) auditor report on systems and procedures; (7) additional ODP-specific information including services, asset classes, trade repository details, settlement arrangements, valuation arrangements, governance arrangements.

sections.title: Information required in respect of members of controlling body
sections.text: Requires per controlling body member: CV with qualifications and experience, criminal/disciplinary history, involvement in business rescue/liquidation, sequestration history, bar from any profession, and disclosure of any pending proceedings.

sections.title: Questionnaire to be completed by members of controlling body or senior managers
sections.text: Personal details questionnaire covering: personal identification, residential history, nationality, qualifications, investment history, and specific fit-and-proper test covering 11 questions about criminal convictions, professional sanctions, licence suspensions, insolvency, debt review, judgment debts, and involvement in entities under business rescue or liquidation.

sections.title: Questionnaire to be completed by the provider entity
sections.text: Entity-level questionnaire: entity name, registration number, registered address, bank and auditor details, confirmation of communication and filing facilities, and financial soundness declaration — assets exceed liabilities, current assets meet current liabilities, no outstanding judgment debts, no liquidation or business rescue.
